fixes.explanation: Right, friend. In verse 33 David says the LORD "…listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people." So the card has it backwards. The LORD does not despise them.

I get the thought, since David says shame has covered his face. But he doesn't ask for anyone to forget him. He prays, "May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me…" That's the request he makes about them.
Yes. David says, "…the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me." The insults against God have fallen on David. I think that's what can happen when you stand close to something you love.
Plenty of us would be tempted to. But look at what the psalm says comes next. After the mocking, David says, "But my prayer to You, O LORD, is for a time of favor." He prays.
Hold on, friend. David never says he's counting on his brothers' prayers. He asks God to answer him "In Your abundant loving devotion…" That's what he points to.
Testing with fire isn't in David's request. He says, "Draw near to my soul and redeem me…" He asks God to come close and redeem him.

That's right. David says, "I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I found no one." He looked for comfort and found none. I think that's one of the loneliest lines in the psalm.
I'd love for the psalm to say that, friend. But David says, "…for comforters, but I found no one." He doesn't say he found a friend there.

That's it. David says his praise "…will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves." In verse 30 he says he will praise God's name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving. I think that tells you a lot about what he treasures.
David says the opposite. In verse 33 he says, "For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people." So the LORD does not despise them.
Rebuild is right. David says, "For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah…" The psalm that started in the mud ends with rebuilding.
